Historical visibility percentile returns the nearest-rank visibility in metres for observed hours. Use it when an agent needs a conservative distribution summary of a station period.
Historical visibility change returns the largest loss of sight distance between consecutive measured hours. Use it when an agent needs a sudden deterioration and its two observed readings.
Historical visibility recovery counts consecutive-hour crossings from at or below a threshold to above it. Use it when an agent needs the first recovery time and number of observed recoveries.
Historical visibility spell analysis returns the longest uninterrupted run at or below a threshold. Use it when an agent needs the duration and endpoints of a low-visibility spell.
Historical visibility frequency measures the share of observed hours at or below a specified distance. Use it when an agent needs the frequency of low visibility at a station.
Historical visibility returns the earliest hourly observation with the minimum sight distance in a UTC period. Use it when an agent needs the worst observed visibility and its measurement time.
Weather history finds the first continuous run in a requested wind sector lasting the specified number of hours. Use it when an agent needs a dated exposure window with an exact minimum duration.
Weather history separates calm observations from measured wind without a direction and gaps in speed. Use it when an agent needs a coverage denominator for directional analyses.
Weather history counts clockwise and counterclockwise turns between adjacent hourly directions. Use it when an agent needs the balance of veering and backing winds.
Weather history estimates the share of observations with a headwind component against a travel bearing. Use it when an agent needs the historical burden of opposing wind.
Weather history counts hourly crosswind components exceeding a threshold relative to a supplied bearing. Use it when an agent needs a retrospective crosswind exposure count.
Weather history returns average wind speeds by the compass sector from which the wind blew. Use it when an agent needs speed differences across directions.
Weather history finds the largest turn between consecutive observed hourly winds. Use it when an agent needs the time and size of an abrupt direction change.
Weather history finds the longest consecutive hourly run in one compass sector. Use it when an agent needs the start and end of a persistent wind direction.
Weather history computes the circular mean and resultant concentration of observed wind directions. Use it when an agent needs a representative direction across the north boundary.
Weather history returns the most frequent eight-point wind direction at a German station. Use it when an agent needs the prevailing wind and the number of tied sectors.
Heating sensitivity measures extra degree days and newly active heating days when the balance point rises. Use it when an agent needs the effect of changing a building balance temperature.
Heating load concentration identifies the month contributing the most degree days in a supplied interval. Use it when an agent needs the share of heating demand concentrated in one month.
Heating site comparison measures the demand difference using only dates observed at both stations. Use it when an agent needs an aligned comparison between two sites.
Metered heating normalization divides supplied heating energy by the measured degree-day total. Use it when an agent needs a weather-normalized energy intensity.
Heating budget history finds the first day cumulative heating demand reached a supplied degree-day target. Use it when an agent needs a threshold date in a complete station record.
Cooling history finds the complete seven-day window with the largest cooling-degree sum. Use it when an agent needs a peak weekly cooling load.
Heating season history finds the longest uninterrupted sequence of below-base daily means. Use it when an agent needs a continuous heating run with dated endpoints.
Building climate history counts heating, cooling and neutral days for a two-threshold control band. Use it when an agent needs the observed duty-day mix.
Heating demand history applies a separate heating cutoff and indoor reference temperature. Use it when an agent needs a degree-day index using a building heating threshold.
Weather history returns heating and cooling degree days at a chosen balance temperature. Use it when an agent needs a thermal load total from measured daily means.
Ground temperature contrast finds the largest observed gap between air and near-ground daily minima. Use it when an agent needs the strongest surface cooling relative to screen height.
Station frost comparison counts matched dates when only one of two locations recorded air frost. Use it when an agent needs a location-specific frost discrepancy.
Frost recurrence counts subzero spells that return after at least one observed frost-free day. Use it when an agent needs the pattern of returning frost.
Frost threshold sensitivity counts extra or excluded cold dates when a buyer changes the air-minimum trigger from zero. Use it when an agent needs the impact of adjusting a cold-weather threshold.
Frost onset comparison returns the first observed ground and air frost and their signed separation in days. Use it when an agent needs the observed lead of ground frost.
Freeze-thaw amplitude reports the widest daily temperature range on a day that crossed the freezing threshold. Use it when an agent needs the sharpest observed same-day freeze and thaw.
Freezing spell search finds the longest uninterrupted span with daily maxima below zero. Use it when an agent needs a persistent ice-day interval.
Frost-free interval search finds the longest uninterrupted span with nonnegative air minima. Use it when an agent needs a contiguous frost-free planning window.
Ground frost comparison counts dates with subzero near-ground minima while the two-metre minimum remained above or at zero. Use it when an agent needs frost missed by an air-temperature-only rule.
Historical frost classification counts ice days, freeze-thaw days and frost-free days using daily air extrema. Use it when an agent needs observed daily freezing regimes.
Historical station pressure variability reports the root-mean-square pressure change over consecutive day pairs. Use it when an agent needs the typical magnitude of pressure movements.
Historical station pressure reversals count strict local peaks and troughs in consecutive daily means. Use it when an agent needs how often the station pressure direction changed.
Historical station pressure stability finds the consecutive three-day window with the smallest high-to-low spread. Use it when an agent needs the steadiest short pressure interval.

Historical station pressure trend fits daily station pressure against elapsed calendar days and reports the residual RMS. Use it when an agent needs a linear drift estimate over a historical interval.
Historical station pressure deficit sums the daily pressure shortfall below a chosen local reference in hPa-days. Use it when an agent needs integrated exposure below a reference pressure.
Historical station pressure threshold crossings count upward and downward breaks of a pressure level on adjacent days. Use it when an agent needs transitions across a locally chosen level.
Historical station pressure change tails locate the largest increase and decrease between consecutive daily means. Use it when an agent needs the extremes of observed day-to-day changes.

Historical station pressure drawdown finds the greatest decline from a preceding observed daily mean within a continuous run and the first recovery day. Use it when an agent needs the path from peak t
Historical station pressure range returns the dates and levels of the lowest and highest daily means. Use it when an agent needs the pressure envelope at one station.
